title: Teemo Attacking
description: Brute force to optimized: marking every individual poisoned second versus a single pass summing capped gaps between attacks.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given a non-decreasing array timeSeries of attack timestamps and an integer duration, each attack poisons the target for exactly duration seconds starting at that timestamp, UNLESS the target is already poisoned, in which case the poison effect is simply extended (not stacked) rather than restarting from scratch or adding extra time. Return the total number of seconds the target is poisoned.

blocks.text: Each attack at time t poisons the target during [t, t+duration). If the next attack happens before this window ends, the poison effect is simply extended (not doubled), so the ACTUAL contribution of that attack to the total poisoned time is only the gap until the next attack, capped at duration.

blocks.title: Analogy: Overlapping Medicine Dosages Extending, Not Stacking, Effect Duration
blocks.text: Picture a medicine whose effect lasts a fixed number of hours after each dose, but taking a new dose while still under effect just extends the current effect rather than adding a second, separate effect period on top. The total time under effect is the sum of each dose's "extension" beyond where the effect already reached.

blocks.caption: Each attack contributes min(duration, gap to next attack) to the total, capping the addition when attacks are close together

blocks.text: Result: 4. Attack at 1 poisons [1,3); attack at 4 poisons [4,6); since the gap (3) exceeds duration (2), there is no overlap, giving 2+2=4 total seconds.

Before marking every individual poisoned second, notice that each attack's TRUE contribution to the total poisoned time is either the full duration (if the next attack is far enough away) or just the gap until the next attack (if it arrives sooner, since the poison window would have been extended rather than stacked).

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: The LAST attack always contributes its full duration, since there is no subsequent attack to cut it short.

Observation 2: For every OTHER attack, its true contribution to the total is the gap to the NEXT attack, capped at duration: if the next attack comes within duration seconds, the poison window is extended by only that gap (before merging into the next attack's window); if it comes later, the full duration counts since the window fully expires.

Observation 3: Summing min(duration, gap to next attack) over all attacks except the last, then adding the full duration for the last attack, gives exactly the total distinct poisoned time.

Observation 4: This requires only a single left-to-right pass over the sorted timestamps, with no need to simulate individual seconds or explicitly merge interval objects.
This leads to a single pass: for each attack except the last, add min(duration, gap to the next attack) to the total; then add the full duration for the last attack.
Mark every poisoned second explicitly (using a set to avoid double-counting overlapping seconds), then count the total marked seconds.

items: For each attack time t, mark every second from t to t+duration-1 as poisoned in a set.
After processing all attacks, the set's size is the total distinct poisoned seconds.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Marking every individual second directly and correctly counts the total distinct poisoned time.
This costs O(n times duration), potentially very slow given duration can be up to 10^7.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n times duration).
Space: O(n times duration) in the worst case, for the set of marked seconds.

Limitation: individually marking every second is unnecessary; the gap between consecutive attacks (capped at duration) directly determines each attack's true contribution, computable in O(n) total without touching individual seconds.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why marking individual seconds is wasteful: only the GAP between consecutive attacks matters for determining overlap, not which specific seconds are poisoned.

The key insight: for each attack except the last, its true contribution to the total poisoned time is min(duration, gap to next attack), since a smaller gap means the poison window gets cut short by the next attack's window taking over.

Handling the last attack: since there is no next attack to cut it short, it always contributes its full duration.

The core idea: a single pass summing min(duration, gap) for each attack except the last, plus the full duration for the last one.
In a single pass over timeSeries, for each attack except the last, add min(duration, timeSeries[i+1] - timeSeries[i]) to the total. Add the full duration for the last attack.

blocks.caption: Sum min(duration, gap to next attack) for each attack except the last, plus full duration for the last

blocks.text: Each attack's poison window either fully expires before the next attack begins (contributing its full duration) or gets subsumed by the next attack's window taking over partway through (contributing only up to that point, the gap). Summing this "capped contribution" across all attacks except the last, and adding the last attack's uninterrupted full duration, exactly reconstructs the total distinct poisoned time without ever needing to consider individual seconds.

blocks.text: Teemo Attacking is a clean example of computing total interval coverage via gap analysis, avoiding the need to simulate or explicitly merge individual time units.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "overlapping fixed-length effects extend rather than stack", think: sum min(duration, gap to next event), with the last event contributing its full duration.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: Marking individual seconds costs O(n times duration) time and space; the single-pass gap analysis costs O(n) time and O(1) space, the standard efficient solution.

items: Pattern: single-pass gap analysis to compute total coverage of overlapping fixed-length windows.
Core Idea: each attack contributes min(duration, gap to next attack); the last attack contributes its full duration.
Time: O(n times duration) for marking individual seconds, O(n) for the optimized gap analysis.
Most Important Observation: overlapping windows extend rather than stack, so only the capped gap to the next event matters.
Interview Difficulty: an accessible interval-coverage problem once the gap-capping insight is recognized.
One line memory trick: sum min(duration, next gap); add full duration for the last attack.
